# PMC3196500 figure reproduction

The pipeline that reruns Thorlund et al. (2011) and compares every printed table cell and every figure panel
with the paper. The method itself is the package [`../package`](../package) (`oisim`); this folder only
drives it and compares.

## What the code does, against the paper

| Paper | Ours | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Trial sizes: an interval drawn with Table S2's "proportions used for simulations" (Cochrane) or 80%/20% on 20-200 and 200-500 ('common'), then a uniform size on it | Same; integer sizes, 201-500 for the second 'common' interval | Appendix S2 |
| n/2 patients per arm, rounded up | Same | Appendix S2 |
| PC_i uniform on 1-5%, 5-15%, 15-40% or 40-80%; ln RR_i ~ N(ln RR, tau²); PE_i = PC_i RR_i | Same; PE_i capped at 1 | Appendix S2 |
| e ~ bin(n_i, P) | Binomial on the arm size (the whole trial size gives 10 of 144 Table 1 cells) | Appendix S2, tested |
| DerSimonian-Laird random-effects model, after each trial | Same, on the log RR; 0.5 added to every cell of a trial with a zero cell; trials with no events in either arm left out | Appendix S1; zero cells our choice |
| 20,000 meta-analyses of 100 trials, 36 scenarios | Same | Methods, Fig. 1 |
| Share of RRR > 20% and > 30% per 500 or 200 patients and 50 or 20 events | Tables: each estimate counts in the interval its cumulative count falls in; spacing 500 patients and 50 events (100 patients for Table S3). Figures: patients by the nearest point, events by the interval; spacing 500 patients (200 for PC 15-80%) and 50 events | Searched (see below) |
| Patients and events for the share to drop below 10%, 5%, 1% | The first point below the level; ">50000" or ">5000" when never | Searched |
| OIS = 4 (z + z)² P(1 − P)/δ² × 1/(1 − I²) | Same, z two-sided for α = 5%; rounding as the printed cells follow it | Methods, Table 2 |

**Searched settings.** The paper does not say how a pooled estimate is assigned to a point of the curve or
how the tables were read off. `tables.py` scores every combination of binning rule (interval, nearest point,
the last or the first trial at an edge), read-off rule (first point below the level, or the point after which
it stays below) and spacing (100, 200, 500 patients; 10, 20, 50 events) against Tables 1, S3 and S4 and uses
the best (`tables.json`, `search`). `figures.py` does the same for the curves, by mean panel score per axis
(`figures.json`, `rule_search`). Both are `found_by_search` assumptions in `results.json`.

## Scoring a figure panel

Each panel's box and tick marks are found in the published image and the pixel map is fitted to the ticks and
their printed labels (log x axis, 1-2-5 ticks; y every 0.05; residuals at most 1.4 px). Our two curves are
drawn on that grid at the published line width and scored both ways with a 2 px tolerance: the share of the
published curve pixels near ours, and of ours near the published ink (dotted and dash-dot lines closed
along x first). The panel's score is the smaller one.

Controls, scored with the same code on the same panel: two wrong inputs (the scenario with the other control
risk range; another tau²) and three near misses (ours ×1.05, ×0.95, shifted one point right). The chance
ceiling is our second run (other seeds) scored against our first. The pass mark is the larger of the best
control plus 0.01 and 90% of the chance ceiling, so a panel agrees only when it beats every control and is
about as close to the paper as our two runs are to each other.

## Layout

| Path | Content |
| --- | --- |
| `main.nf`, `nextflow.config` | The pipeline. |
| `requirements.txt` | Pinned Python packages (Python 3.12). |
| `results_notes.json` | What a person writes: labels, assumptions, the causes of the tables, the page's prose. Numbers are cited as `{facts}` filled from the run. |
| `results.json` | The repository's results-check file (every compared value of the run), written by `make_results_check.py`. |
| `published/` | Fig. 2 and Figs S1-S12 as lossless PNGs of the published files (CC BY; see its README). |
| `pipeline/fetch_inputs.sh` | Downloads the figure files, Tables S3-S4 and the article XML (PMC on AWS; Europe PMC as fallback) and checks their SHA-256. |
| `pipeline/verify_published.py` | Checks that `published/` decodes to the downloaded figures pixel for pixel (Fig. 2 is skipped, with a note, when Europe PMC is down and the smaller AWS copy was fetched instead). |
| `pipeline/extract_published.py` | Reads the printed tables into `output/published_values.json` (with `--extract`; needs LibreOffice). |
| `pipeline/simulate.py` | All 36 scenarios with `oisim`, a second run with other seeds, and two hypothesis variants on the Cochrane scenarios. |
| `pipeline/tables.py` | The read-off search, Tables 1, S3, S4, Table 2, the OIS columns of Tables 3 and 4, and the range rules tried on Tables 3 and 4. |
| `pipeline/figures.py` | Every panel drawn on its published grid, scored with its controls; renders and overlays. |
| `pipeline/claims.py` | The text's statements on the paper's own tables and on ours. |
| `pipeline/build_results.py`, `check_results.py` | `../results.json` and its verdicts. |
| `pipeline/build_page.py`, `page_template.html` | The results page (`site/PMC3196500/`). |
| `pipeline/check_reproduction.py`, `compare_runs.py` | The fresh run against the committed outputs. |
| `pipeline/check_package.py` | Builds and tests `oisim` in a fresh environment and reruns its tutorial. |
| `pipeline/update_readmes.py` | The results tables of the READMEs. |
| `output/` | What the pipeline writes: `simulation.json` (counts per point for every scenario, rule and spacing), `tables.json`, `figures.json`, `claims.json`, `published_values.json`, `package.json`, `fig*_ours.png` and `fig*_overlay.png`. |

## Run

From the repository root:

```bash
pip install -r PMC3196500/figure-reproduction/requirements.txt ./PMC3196500/package
nextflow run PMC3196500/figure-reproduction/main.nf --outdir results
```

About 4 minutes on 4 cores (the simulation takes 2.5). `--workers N` sets the processes of the simulation;
`--sources DIR` reuses local downloads; `--extract` reads the printed tables again (LibreOffice).

## Pipeline steps

1. `FETCH`: downloads and SHA-256; the committed published figures checked against them.
2. `PUBLISHED_VALUES`: the printed tables (committed copy, or extracted again with `--extract`).
3. `SIMULATE`: 36 scenarios + 36 with other seeds + 2 × 12 variants, 20,000 meta-analyses of 100 trials each.
4. `TABLES`, `FIGURES`, `CLAIMS`: the comparisons.
5. `PACKAGE`: `check_package.py` on `../package`.
6. `RESULTS`: `results.json` with computed verdicts, the results-check file, the page, and `check_reproduction.py`.
7. `CHECK`: fails if `check_results.py` fails, a verdict changes, or any output differs from the committed one
   (numbers within 1e-9, images by pixels; `package.json` holds timings and is left out).

## Limits

- The simulation is stochastic and the paper gives no seeds, so no cell can be expected to match by more
  than chance allows; our own two runs agree on 59% to 86% of the read-off cells.
- The binning and read-off rules are searched, not stated: a different rule moves every read-off by up to a
  bin.
- The zero-cell rule, integer trial sizes and the cap of PE at 1 are our choices. The zero-cell rule was
  tested on Table 1: keeping double-zero trials changes the exact count by 1 (82 against 81).
- Scratch tests outside the pipeline (not rerun): on the Cochrane scenarios with PC 1-5% and 5-15%, tau² 0.05,
  leaving out one-trial meta-analyses, a 0.1 correction, leaving out every trial with a zero cell, and bins
  offset by 100 to 200 patients were tried; none brought both the 500 and the 2,000 patient points of
  the curves to the published values.
- Tables 3 and 4's simulation columns are not compared: no rule rebuilds them from the paper's own tables.
- Tables S1 and S2 and Fig. S13 summarize a survey of Cochrane reviews that are not listed.
